In 1990, USA Today formally contacted NASA to clarify rumors about their latest technology, apparently dubbed “sex packets.” Weeks prior, Oakland’s afrosurrealist rap collective Digital Underground (DU) had released their debut album, Sex Packets, themed around a new drug for astronauts that could instantly gratify their sexual desires. As DU’s transgressive lyrics glorified the illicit substance, news of the invention leaked onto the Bay Area’s streets: pamphlets were distributed, and condoms were passed out. NASA was forced to respond to the coital discourse: “NASA has not in the past, nor will they in the future, be working on such a pill … It would be impossible to satisfy the carnal urges of astronauts … To my knowledge, unbridled lust has never interfered with a space mission.” It’s the first and likely last instance of NASA being outmaneuvered by Oakland rappers. (It turned out DU had created the pamphlets and condoms as subversive promotional materials.) The elaborate prank was a piece of artistic genius orchestrated by Gregory Jacobs — the late MC, songwriter, illustrator, pianist and costume-wearing virtuoso known as Shock G. The NASA incident is just one of the many shenanigans detailed in his posthumous memoir, Keep It Beautiful: Inside the Funkyverse of Shock G and Digital Underground, out Aug. 25 — Shock G’s birthday — from Penguin Random House. The book combines handwritten notes, interview transcripts, personal photos and rare sketches compiled by Jacobs’ longtime friend and photographer, Alexis Wolfe Mbassa, who tagged along with Jacobs in order to document his eccentric life for over a decade. The association was intentional; in 2011, Jacobs personally recruited Wolfe Mbassa as a co-author for his autobiography. In 2021, just eight months after submitting the book to literary agents, Jacobs died from a drug overdose in Florida. He was 57. “It was never about money or becoming successful for him; it was about having the freedom to create,” Wolfe Mbassa told KQED. “He put himself in wild situations just to hold on to that freedom.” Wild situations form much of Keep It Beautiful. It details Jacobs’ stints in pimping, homelessness and jail, while containing all of the exuberant, out-of-pocket abundance of a Shock G production. A conversation between Shock G and George Clinton of Parliament Funkadelic? Yup. An African gray parrot named Afro who lives in Shock G’s childhood home and imitates his stepmom, Sonya? That too. One entire chapter is dedicated to his early friendship with a teenage Tupac Shakur, who joined DU as a member before going solo. (Apparently Pac had a “fucked” jump shot in basketball, and no one wanted him on their team). Largely stream-of-consciousness in homage to Jacobs’ creative process, the book is divided into sections based on the regions where he lived. Wolfe Mbassa traveled to each of them to conduct interviews: Topanga Canyon, Hollywood, Los Angeles, Oakland, New York City and Tampa. Jacobs recounts his first job as a 15-year-old, DJing at a local radio station in Tampa. He was fired for disobeying the radio’s directives and opting to spin the full 15-minute version of “(Not Just) Knee Deep” by Funkadelic instead of airing commercials. It isn’t the only example in the book of his natural inclination to rebel. Jacobs extensively details how he evaded authorities, and circumvented court appearances, from age 17 to 22. Even for the most studious hip-hop heads, Keep It Beautiful reveals overlooked wrinkles in Shock’s personality and biography. (Did you know that DU’s original band name was “Spice Regime”?) The book also includes a trove of never-before-seen drawings by Jacobs, showcasing a crude and whimsical style that would come to define his artistry, which sometimes reached ridiculous levels of raunch. (One sketch portrays an anthropomorphic anus forcing an “ASS-PIRIN” pill down its own hole.) But the main thrust of Keep It Beautiful are the granular narratives that Jacobs discloses, like his memories of being jailed in San Diego for six months for grand theft auto, where he used art as a bartering tool. In scattered, disconnected bursts, he and Wolfe Mbassa recount his side quests and failures (such as his brief time as a male “gigolo” in Pennsylvania) revealing the down-bad experiences that molded his worldview before his rap and art careers took off. Glimpses of that fast life can be heard in his lyrics, but the book shows in detail how Shock G actually did get around from coast to coast. At its core, the collage of archival material shows how music and art became Jacobs’ salvation, therapy and refuge. Putting it all together was a joyous challenge for Wolfe Mbassa, personally tasked by Jacobs to retain the book’s silliness and humor. “One of the most difficult parts was trying to figure out how to pull all the pieces together. He always wanted it to be like a scrapbook,” she says. “He wanted it to feel like his personal journals did: stories, mixed with memorabilia and art.” In sitting with Keep It Beautiful, its spiritual thesis is clear: Jacobs’ everlasting search for beauty, creativity and funky originality shone brightest during his darkest hours. It’s about keeping it beautiful, especially when beauty isn’t easily kept. “It was so much fun,” Wolfe Mbassa confirms, “to live in his world.” ‘Keep It Beautiful: Inside the Funkyverse of Shock G and Digital Underground’ will be released on Aug. 25. A free release party with Alexis Wolfe Mbassa and members of Digital Underground takes place Saturday, Aug. 22 at Drake’s Dealership (2325 Broadway, Oakland). Event information here.

title: What Do We Make Of Karol G’s ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’ Top 10 Debut? - Billboard
content: This week's Five Burning Questions looks at Karol G's No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, which also dethrones Bad Bunny on the Top Latin Albums chart this week. Throughout her career, Karol G has typically taken a couple of years between her albums. So, when she announced her sixth studio set would arrive just over one year after her last album, 2025’s Tropicoqueta, it was a bit of a surprise. Especially considering she announced the new album just one week before its Aug. 7 release. No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto debuts at No. 8 on the all-genre Billboard 200 — her fourth top 10 debut. The album opens with 50,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States in the tracking week of Aug. 7-13, according to Luminate. Meanwhile, the set debuts at No. 1 on Top Latin Albums, her fifth straight debut at the chart’s summit. Album standouts include the Drake collaboration, “Ahí,” which debuts atop Hot Latin Songs, and the Bruno Mars-assisted “Still,” which earns this album its highest-charting Hot 100 entry, as it enters at No. 41. Both the album and “Ahí” dethrone Bad Bunny on Top Latin Albums (ending his 77-nonconsecutive-week reign) and on Hot Latin Songs (ending his 72-nonconsecutive-week-reign). So, how do those No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto stats compare with our expectations? And will the album’s “Ahí” become a lasting chart hit? Billboard staffers discuss these questions and more below. Cata Balzano: I’m not surprised it didn’t debut in the top five, given how the announcement unfolded. It felt organic and aligned with the growing trend of artists using the opportunity to address thousands of fans and reveal that new music is on the way, often keeping the next project under wraps. There were only nine days between the announcement on July 29 and the album’s release on Aug. 7. Given how sentimental, personal and introspective the album is, that may have been part of the strategy: releasing it when it felt right, rather than waiting until enough promotion had been done to ensure everyone knew about it and tuned in. Even so, it still debuted in the top 10 — a testament to Carolina’s status as one of the biggest Latin superstars of the moment. At this point, Carolina does what Carolina wants. Lyndsey Havens: A bit below! I think of Karol as such a hitmaker, and I thought given the momentum of a headlining Coachella set into her last album Tropicoqueta (which only dropped last summer) into a stadium tour would have warranted a bigger debut week – especially when you consider that she only announced this album a week before its release. But, such a brief rollout runway can equally present opportunities and challenges, and it seems that it was perhaps more of a challenge this time around. That said, she still secured a top 10 debut despite any challenges, which is still cause for celebration. Isabela Raygoza: Personally, it landed slightly below my expectations — and that’s not to say it’s a bad album! I just think audiences were more accustomed to Karol G’s celebratory, high-energy Latin-driven sound. Opening in the Top 10 of the Billboard 200 with 50,000 units is still a solid result and speaks to the strength of her fan base. But compared with the massive success of Mañana Será Bonito (No. 1) and Tropicoqueta (No. 3), it feels a bit like a soft landing than the blockbuster opening we might have expected. Sigal Ratner-Arias: Slightly worse. Given the track record of Karol’s last albums and her current stadium tour, I was expecting another top 5 — especially with collaborators as big as Drake and Bruno Mars. Jessica Roiz: Following her past three albums, Mañana Será Bonito (2023) which debuted No. 1, and both Mañana Será Bonito (Bichota Season) (2023) and Tropicoqueta (2025) at No. 3, I expected No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto to debut in the Top 5 at least. However, a Top 10 debut is not too shabby — and it’s still a remarkable achievement for a primarily all-Spanish-language album. Cata Balzano: I believe it came down to the marketing. Both Tropicoqueta and Mañana Será Bonito appeared to have larger marketing and promotional campaigns, with months of support across various platforms, including her social media accounts. By contrast, this album arrived on the heels of a major promotional campaign for the Viajando Por El Mundo Tropicoqueta Tour, which became the top marketing priority from the moment La Bichota announced it. I also believe Tropicoqueta and No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto evoke two completely opposite moods. I’m not sure listeners were ready to move from such a high-energy salsa, merengue and tropical vibe to a low-key, moody “sad girl summer.” That may have also contributed to the shift we saw. Lyndsey Havens: I always love when an album comes at you fast — and a one-week rollout is surely speedy. But, I think it’s also really difficult to properly set up a project in that amount of time — especially when the artist is amidst a massive tour and perhaps limited in the kind of promotional appearances they can do that would otherwise accompany an album rollout. But I think we also have to take into account the overall inspiration and theme of this album, which boasts a title that translates to “I don’t regret feeling so much.” It is indeed an album of big feels, and as such the tempo is a bit slower and softer than what we’ve come to know from La Bichota. So I think while this album didn’t have as high a debut as her previous two, I’d bet that it may have accomplished more for her emotionally – and that seems to have been the point. Isabela Raygoza: I think the biggest factor was the rollout strategy. Karol G built anticipation for both Mañana Será Bonito and Tropicoqueta with well-timed teases that aligned with each album’s cultural moment. By contrast, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto arrived as a sharper left turn: a personal heartbreak record released amid the celebratory, tropical spectacle of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, complete with fruit-inspired visuals and colorful feathered costumes and headpieces. This latest album is more of a headphone listen than a stadium soundtrack. Sigal Ratner-Arias: I think the timing for this album wasn’t 100% right. Although I did enjoy it quite a bit, with a much more mellow tone than her previous works No Me Arrepiento doesn’t really feel like a summer album. Jessica Roiz: She announced this album one week in advance, and truthfully, I feel like nobody was expecting it. She also announced it first to about 50,000 people at a stadium show in Canada, as opposed to making a wider announcement on her social media, where she amasses millions of fans from all over the world. Meanwhile, for both Mañana Será Bonito and Tropicoqueta, she had an entire promo plan that began at least a month before their releases, creating that expectation and an actual countdown. Also, fans were really eager to find out what she would sing about in both albums: the former spotlighted her healing process following a very public breakup from Puerto Rican rapper Anuel AA, and the latter was created during the time she dated Colombian singer Feid. NMADST shows a now healed, single, and confident Karol embracing her emotions and living in the present. Cata Balzano: Not only do we have Drake — who made Billboard chart history this year by becoming the first artist to simultaneously claim the top three spots on the Billboard 200 with a synchronized triple-album release, proving he’s still got it — but he’s also singing in Spanish and putting his own spin on the song by weaving his “New Bestie” verse into the track. It’s the perfect blend of Karol’s romantic reggaetón and Drake’s flirtatious Champagne Papi charisma. For those who understand the lyrics, the song is also deeply relatable: having a love interest while being emotionally unavailable and asking that person to hang in there as you move through the stages of healing after a breakup is the perfect theme for an album that explores heartbreak so profoundly. Lyndsey Havens: Of course, we have to account for Drake’s clout here. At the very least, I think seeing his name on the tracklist warranted some curiosity listens — especially once word spread he was singing in Spanish, too. But it’s also a genuinely catchy song with a great beat that contrasts some slower moments like the two songs that immediately follow: “Still” and “Final feliz.” I’m pleasantly surprised by this collab, and just as surprised that it was the one to bump Bad Bunny — kudos to you, Karol. Isabela Raygoza: Drake’s fan base is a huge part of it, but the song also had the novelty of being their first official collaboration with Karol G. “Ahí” is easy to replay, with a flirtatious back-and-forth that makes it earwormy than just another album cut. After 72 weeks of “DtMF” at No. 1, listeners were probably ready for a fresh song with that kind of star power and crossover appeal. Sigal Ratner-Arias: I attribute this, in large part, to the Drake factor. Drake not only has a huge following in his native tongue, but also among Hispanics. Over the years, he’s been catering to them too with strategic collaborations, including with Bad Bunny (“Mía”, “Gently”), Romeo Santos (“Odio”) and Chino Pacas & Fuerza Regida (“Modo Capone”), among others. Furthermore, it is one of the most upbeat songs on the album, and both artists’ voices complement each other really well. Jessica Roiz: I mean, it’s Drake…singing in Spanish. Though it’s not his first rodeo singing in Spanish (he previously did so with Bad Bunny on “Mía”), I think his massive star power will always speak volumes…in any language, in any chart. Cata Balzano: I understand why it had its highest Hot 100 debut, because another major global artist is featured on it, but I don’t consider it will become a growing hit. The song, which has Bruno’s DNA in the rhythms and style, shows Karol’s versatility and abiloty to adapt to another artist’s blueprint style, but it doesn’t feel like a hit song that I’d want to have on repeat in my playlist. At least not right now — maybe in the winter, when cozy seasonal blues kick in, I’ll change my mind. Lyndsey Havens: Bruno Mars has a magic sauce when it comes to collaborations, including more downtempo tracks like this one – look no further than his duet with Lady Gaga, “Die With a Smile,” for proof. While “Still” isn’t an obvious hit to me, especially if I’m comparing it to something a bit more uptempo like “Ahí,” I can totally see it being a slow grower. And I think with time, the lyrics (especially the chorus, on which she sings “’cause I’d still love you/ Even with a broken heart”) will hit even harder. All this song needs is one epic live performance to push it up the chart. Fortunately, they are both pros when it comes to delivering just that. Isabela Raygoza: I could see “Still” growing, especially with Bruno Mars’ mesmerizing voice and the song’s nostalgic, ’80s-inspired power-ballad sheen. The emotional hook — “I still love you even with a broken heart” — is immediate, and Karol has previously said the song expressed exactly what she was feeling. That said, her English delivery may feel less natural to some English-language-dominant listeners, which could limit its crossover potential; Bruno’s sections are the undeniable standout. Sigal Ratner-Arias: It’s hard to say. Although this is not Karol’s first song primarily in English — in 2021 she recorded the more upbeat hit “Don’t Be Shy” with Tiësto — I think this song would have worked more on her favor in Spanish. Vocally, I also feel like Bruno Mars really stands out here. But Karol does show a new side of her and new colors of her voice which are sweet to the ear. Jessica Roiz: I’m not sure how I feel about “Still” quite yet. I was expecting something completely different in terms of rhythm, perhaps a sly funk blended with a provocative reggaetón, but the ‘80s power ballad approach really took me off guard. It gave me “Wedding Singer” vibes at first. The lyrics, I love, the harmonies, I love, and at the end of the day, they are singing about a very relatable topic; however, I’m not sure what its future holds. Instead, I see Kaorl’s “BbY WOW” with Judeline and Rusowksy becoming a growing hit — it’s currently the fan favorite on social media. A bop. Cata Balzano: It’s such an effective way to deliver the news directly to the target audience. The people attending the tour are the ones spending money and signing up for presale waiting lists to hear the music live, and they’re likely to be the same fans streaming the album and buying its various physical editions, including vinyl. So it makes sense that artists would want to do something special for their fans and give them the news first. Lyndsey Havens: While fun for fans – especially if the artist incorporates new songs into the set list — I imagine that it’s incredibly difficult for the artist to pull off. At the least, it requires extra time and attention that already seems limited while on a major tour — and at the most, it requires the artist to fluctuate mentalities between more lived in material and music that likely feels much more raw. Depending on the artist, I’d guess that it benefits the tour, by way of generating new buzz, more than the album itself… But of course, artists who are guaranteed a No. 1 debut like Taylor and Ariana can reap the benefits on both ends. I’m really fascinated, and even proud, that Karol went there as well, and do think it could prove to an even wider pool of artists that it can be done. Isabela Raygoza: I think more artists may try it because touring gives them a built-in audience and a direct way to introduce new music. But it’s also a risky move: the album has to fit the tour’s existing energy, and fans may need time to connect with it. In Karol’s case, releasing a more intimate project during such a colorful, joyous tour makes the contrast especially interesting. Sigal Ratner-Arias: It may be a good strategy to introduce new songs to the mix while you have your audience’s attention, and people who’ve already seen the show may try to see it again if there’s a real big hit added to the setlist. But most artists may not have the time, the energy or the bandwidth to record and tour the globe simultaneously, so I don’t expect this to be a trend that many will be able to or interested in following. Jessica Roiz: It’s definitely a trend and I don’t doubt it’s a great strategy, but personally, I don’t think I’ve seen this happening much in the Latin music space. I feel that many artists would rather keep a traditional touring format, such as Romeo Santos and Prince Royce who are touring to promote their joint album and not truly surprising fans with more new music. I’m still curious as to why Karol took this approach for this new album, as opposed to announcing at the end of her trek, but hey, at least she’s spicing up the set list! Earlier this month, in the midst of touring her Tropicoquetta album, Colombian superstar Karol G unexpectedly released No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, which translates to I Don’t Regret Feeling So Much. The title is an almost perfect thesis for the album: moody, raw, and unfiltered. There are melancholic ballads, including “Después de Ti,” her collaboration with Greg Gonzales of the pop band Cigarettes After Sex, alongside more unruly anthems like “Matadora,” or “Killer.” Fans had reason to suspect something new was coming. Months before the surprise album’s release, Karol began dropping beauty-related hints (unsurprising, as she’s someone known for playing with her hair colors and nails). In January, she posted a carousel on Instagram—including an image of herself wearing rhinestones across her forehead and a baby-blue manicure— captioned: “Unfocused But SparkLYYYY.” It was easy to write it off, as she was in the midst of building the world around her album Tropicoquetta. And in April, at the end of her historic Coachella set, Karol announced she was taking Tropicoquetta on the road. The resulting tour, Viajando Por El Mundo—or Traveling Around the World—seemed poised to continue the same visual language: flowers, fiery colors, and plenty of tropical extravagance. The cover art for “No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto.” But there was another clue for both her new album and “sentimental-blue” era. In one of the promotional videos for the tour, Karol opens a suitcase. Sparkles spill out. She looks at them and says, “No, I’m not packing that one yet.” It was a blink-and-you-miss-it moment, but it now feels like a preview of what was coming. The aesthetic of No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto could hardly be more different from Tropicoquetta. One is fluorescent, maximalist, and celebratory; the other is somber, introspective, and stripped back. On the album cover, Karol appears almost makeup-free and bathed in a cool blue hue—giving the image a nostalgic vibe reminiscent of Britney Spears 2003 album, In The Zone. For Karol, color has always been part of the storytelling, according to Duván Foronda, her makeup artist of nearly a decade. “She is someone who puts color to everything; for her, a song has a color; for her, a feeling has a color.” When they were creating Tropicoquetta, that feeling was happiness. “She said, ‘I want an album that’s really tropical, that feels really happy.’ And to her, the color that expressed that was orange,” Foronda recounts. The beauty followed suit. “That album had a really defined aesthetic,” he says. “In terms of the makeup, we did a lot of red lips, brown lip liner, and orange tinted cheeks.” Now, he’s helping Karol strip things back. Duván, whom Karol affectionately calls “Duvi,” has been part of the process of bringing the singer closer to a more natural version of herself. It’s an interesting evolution for an artist whose beauty identity has always been playful. Karol performing in Los Angeles for her “Viajando Por El Mundo” tour. Before joining Karol’s world, Foronda followed in the footsteps of his mother, Adriana Pérez, a notable Colombian makeup artist. He assisted her on various jobs before eventually building a career of his own, including working with lingerie brand Leonisa—comparable to Victoria’s Secret— which is one of Colombia’s most recognizable brands. There’s something fitting about Karol entrusting this particular beauty transformation to someone who understands the visual language of Colombian beauty from the inside out. For this era, though, the inspiration came from somewhere else entirely: Hawaii. During the trip, Foronda noticed Karol gravitating toward blue. “I noticed she started wearing a lot of blue,” he says. Eventually, she told Foronda why. “She told me, ‘I don't know, this new era, which is more mine, more vulnerable, more personal, feels blue.’” Soon, the color began appearing everywhere. “We would go out with her, and she would wear a blue shirt, sometimes a blue purse, or even a blue phone case,” Foronda recalls. But this isn’t an electric cobalt or the kind of neon blue that might have felt at home in the Tropicoquetta universe. It’s softer, airier. “You’ll notice it's not a vibrant blue; it's like a sky-blue,” he says. “It’s calming.” That sense of calm is starting to make its way onto the stage, too. On her Viajando Por El Mundo tour, which recently stopped in Los Angeles for three sold-out shows with special guests including Becky G and Bruno Mars, the energy of this newer era exists alongside the tropical spectacle that fans have gotten to know. “In the show, we’re still doing the Tropicoquetta [aesthetic], but we’re starting to add some new touches,” Foronda says. “We’re adding Swarovski crystals in her makeup, adding glitter to her makeup, and we’re also doing darker makeup.” It’s the “moodier” makeup, however, that is the biggest departure for the Colombian singer, says Foronda. “In this new era, we’ll see her with makeup that’s darker, riskier,” he explains. The deeper, more undone looks are meant to reveal another side of Karol: the rebellious one. The key to this look is a smudgy eyeliner. “It has to be messy; it can’t be glam or perfect, like a perfect line,” says Foronda. And if that feels like a rejection of the pristine, hyper-polished beauty which has dominated our feeds for years, that’s because it is— at least a little bit. After spending recent years embracing her natural beauty and the soft-focus appeal of “clean girl” makeup, Karol is embracing the mess. More eyeliner. More glitter. More crystals. More drama. The clean girls, it seems, are in fact getting glittery. Bruno Mars joining Karol on-stage during her "Viajando Por El Mundo" tour in Los Angeles. Foronda’s inspiration board for this new direction is equally sparkly. “I get a lot of inspiration from Zara Larsson’s makeup artist, Sophia [Sinot],” he says. “I love all the glitter she uses, and the little rhinestones she adds to the eyes. I love all the glitter she adds to her body.” His technique is refreshingly low-tech. “I bought an [eyeshadow] palette, and I mix it with body lotion.” The eyeshadow palette is from a New Zealand-based brand, “Question Beauty” while a new MIM body lotion—Foronda’s makeup brand— inspired by a lyric in Karol’s song “Ivonny Bonita” is expected to launch soon and will be available worldwide. Of course, underneath all that glitter is skincare. Before a show, skin prep takes priority. Foronda’s secret weapon is a 15-minute Medicube Booster Pro massage that provides temporary rejuvenating effects through LED, microcurrent, sonic vibration, and EMS (electric muscle stimulation), alongside the MIM Hydrating Gel, which contains hyaluronic acid and vitamin B5. Afterward, it’s all about removing what went on. According to Foronda, Karol swears by the MIM Gentle Makeup Remover, particularly when it comes to the layers of mascara required for a stage performance. “For a show, you have to wear a lot of makeup, and that includes heavy mascara,” he says. “And she would always [accidentally] take off all her eyelashes when taking off her makeup.” Now, the remover has become a permanent fixture in Karol’s kit. “She would tell me, ‘There’s no makeup remover like this one.” It’s a small detail, but it captures the beauty philosophy behind this new chapter: the drama can be taken off. The rhinestones can come off. The glitter can be washed away. What remains underneath is the person Karol has been trying to get closer to all along. title: GS Points Leaders Seek Bounce Back This Weekend at VIR - sportscar365.com
content: With new co-driver, McCumbee McAleer Racing looking to return to form this weekend at VIR… The IMSA Michelin Pilot Challenge GS championship leaders look to rebound from abnormal Road America results for the Virginia Is For Racing Lovers Grand Prix at Virginia International Raceway. Robert Noaker will share the No. 13 McCumbee McAleer Racing Ford Mustang GT4 with new co-driver Finn Wiebelhaus starting at VIR. The No. 13 car has finished in the top 11 in each of the first seven races and built its championship lead from 30 points to 100 entering VIR. Ford scored a pair of podiums at VIR last year in the hands of KohR Motorsports, finishing second and third behind eventual season champions Luca Mars and Jan Heylen in the RS1 Porsche 718 GT4 RS CS. Each of the top five in the championship all finished seventh or worse in the Road America 120. That brought a sixth possible GS title contender into play, in the form of series newcomers YRB Racing and Road America winners Trenton Estep and Allen Patten in their No. 66 Aston Martin Vantage AMR GT4 Evo. The second consecutive first-time GS winners have ascended to sixth and only 190 points out of the lead. A second successive win would propel this team even closer to the front of the pack only a handful of races after debuting at Watkins Glen International following an acquisition of van der Steur Racing. But winning this season has not necessarily been a good thing for GS winners in their next race. In an odd quirk, the results for GS winners in their next race, starting at Sebring, have been 29th, ninth, second, fourth, 21st and 28th, for an average 15th place finish. The gap from first to 15th place in IMSA’s scoring system is, conveniently, 190 points. Mars and Dillon Machavern rebounded with a seventh place in their No. 95 Turner Motorsport BMW M4 GT4 EVO to jump back to second in points. They’re tied with fellow BMW runners Stevan McAleer and Austin Krainz in their No. 27 AutoTechnic Racing BMW and 10 points clear of fourth-placed Michael Cooper and Moisey Uretsky in the No. 44 Ibiza Farm Motorsport McLaren Artura GT4. Winward Racing’s Bryce Ward completes the top five, 160 back, in his No. 57 Mercedes-AMG GT GT4. TCR has, on paper, been a bit more straightforward. The Mason Filippi and Bryson Morris pair secured their sixth podium from seven 2026 starts aboard the No. 33 Bryan Herta Autosport Hyundai Elantra N TCR. They hold a 150-point lead on teammates Preston Brown and Denis Dupont, who share the No. 76 Hyundai. Either or both of these two need a big VIR result to make inroads on the Nos. 33 and 76 cars, which appear set to vie for the title in the last three races. Among the 42 cars split 29 GS and 13 TCR, there are several other changes. CarBahn’s No. 39 BMW is absent this race. CSM now switches to Aston Martin for its two entries, and its second car features Ismaeel Ellahi graduating from IMSA VP Racing SportsCar Challenge alongside Ayrton Houk. Kingpin Racing makes its second start of the season with Patrick Wilmot and Tyler Hoffman. Celso Neto and Eddie Gou, who finished second in TCR at Road America in the No. 55 Gou Racing w/Stallion Audi RS 3 LMS TCR, switch to the No. 77 Stallion Motorsports w/GOU CUPRA Leon VZ TCR this race. title: No Regrets, Just No. 1s: Karol G’s ‘No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto’ Debuts Atop Top Latin Albums Chart - Billboard
content: The singer claims her fifth leader on the tally and impacts the Hot Latin Songs chart. Sr. Charts & Data Analyst (Latin & Billboard Español) Karol G’s sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto, debuts at No. 1 on Billboard’s Top Latin Albums chart (dated Aug. 22), halting Bad Bunny’s reign with Debí Tirar Más Fotos, which has spent a record 77 nonconsecutive weeks atop the list and has been No. 1 since the Jan. 24-dated chart. Karol G’s set also floods Hot Latin Songs with 13 entries, led by “Ahí,” with Drake, which opens at No. 1. No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto was released Aug. 7 via Bichota/Interscope/Capitol, just more than a year after Tropicoqueta led the Top Latin Albums chart for two weeks in July 2025. The new set marks Karol G’s fifth straight debut at the summit among seven career entries — only Unstoppable and Ocean fell short, peaking at No. 2 in 2017 and 2019, respectively. No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto begins with 50,000 equivalent album units earned in the United States in the tracking week of Aug. 7-13, according to Luminate. For its chart debut, the set registered 48,000 from streaming activity, which equals to 49.5 million official on-demand streams. Album sales comprised a little over 1,000 units, with a negligible number of track-equivalent units. With No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, Karol G adds her fifth No. 1 on Top Latin Albums. No other female artist has dominated the overall Latin albums ranking in the past decade like Karol G, who trails only the late Jenni Rivera and Shakira, each with seven No. 1 albums, the most among female artists in the chart’s history, dating to 1993. Meanwhile, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto opens at No. 8 on the all-genre Billboard 200 — Karol G’s fourth top 10 — and breaks through to No. 1 on Top Latin Pop Albums. Plus, the set arrives at No. 7 on Top Streaming Albums. Here’s a rundown of Karol G’s No. 1s on Top Latin Albums: On the tracks front, 13 tracks from the new album join two already charting titles on Hot Latin Songs, which includes streaming data, radio airplay and digital sales into its formula. “Después de Ti,” with duet parter Greg González, and the album’s first charting track, flies 17-10, while fellow advance single “Matadora” slips 4-3. But the biggest winner is “Ahí,” her collab with Drake, which debuts at No. 1 largely by 5.9 million official U.S. clicks. The sum yields a No. 46 start on the overall Streaming Songs chart, and a No. 1 on Latin Streaming Songs. title: Biz Buzz: St. G’s Bodega moving into old hardware store in St. Cloud's East End - St. Cloud Live

ST. CLOUD — A new bodega store, St. G’s Bodega, is scheduled to open in early September on the site of an old hardware store in St. Cloud’s East End. It’ll have staple grocery items with a “New York bodega style,” St. G’s Bodega co-owner Maddie Waseka said. That means sodas, cereals, chips, cigarettes and more will all be for sale. “We wanted to add something that was a little bit higher-end than your standard grocery in looks and offered the everyday staples that people need on that side of town,” Waseka said. The location is 415 E St. Germain St., originally the old Sentinel Hardware building before it was purchased by Marla Waseka, Maddie’s mother, in 2022. The Waseka family, through their real estate restoration company, MoXie Ladies, has for years been purchasing dilapidated real estate on 
    
      St. Cloud’s East End,
    
       or areas centered around East St. Germain Street and the Lincoln Avenue corridors, east of the Mississippi River. The long-closed hardware store now houses 
    
      Respect Fight Club
    
       gym in the basement, breakfast and lunch restaurant 
    
      Kitchenette,
    
       home goods store 
    
      Sage & Salvage,
    
       four apartments and now St. G’s Bodega. Nearby, they also purchased the former Ace Bar building on June 26 with plans to restore it as a bar and restaurant. “It's more of a passion project than anything,” Maddie Waseka said. “We figure if we keep doing our own thing and put cool things in, people will come along behind us and do their own cool things on the East Side.” The St. Cloud Retired and Senior Volunteering Program is receiving a $425,000 continuation grant as part of AmeriCorps’ grant competition for organizations that offer volunteer opportunities for people 55 and older. RSVP
    
       is an AmeriCorps program dedicated to seniors hosted by the City of St. Cloud that serves Benton, Sherburne, Stearns and Wright counties. The program matches seniors with volunteer opportunities that match their interests, skills and schedules. The organization’s 1,200 volunteers have worked alongside more than 160 partner nonprofits, government agencies and healthcare groups. “We’re thrilled to be able to continue serving our communities,” RSVP Director Jennifer Wucherer said in a statement. “We are passionate about working with older adults — not only to help meet community needs, but also to honor and value the experience, knowledge and impact that older adults bring. Service is one of the greatest gifts we can offer and one of the more reliable ways to enrich our own well-being.” Around 130 grants were handed out nationally in 2026, with St. Cloud being one of five organizations in Minnesota to receive the award. St. Cloud Financial Credit Union Executive Vice President Chase Larson, who is also the company’s chief lending officer, is the newest member of the Central Minnesota Habitat for Humanity’s board of directors. The board is responsible for ensuring good financial stewardship and accountability. Chad Bouley, executive director for the local branch, said Larson brings sound business leadership to the organization. “Chase is a proven leader in our community, and his vision, creativity, and passion for serving others will be tremendous assets as we continue to grow our impact. We are excited to have him helping shape the future of our organization and advancing our mission throughout Central Minnesota,” Bouley said in a statement. Central Minnesota Habitat for Humanity and St. Cloud Financial Credit Union have partnered on projects before. Central Minnesota Habitat for Humanity named SCFCU as its 2024 Business Partner of the Year. St. Cloud State University recently won a $135,000 state grant to partner with local machining manufacturer Park Industries to boost workforce development training. That figure rises even higher thanks to an additional $262,000 in matching funds from Park Industries to St. Cloud State’s Professional and Continuing Education (PACE) division. The two-year project will involve customized training, leadership development and digital skills training for 217 employees. The grant supports a "robust" training model designed to address workforce challenges in advanced manufacturing, including skills gaps, leadership readiness, digital transformation and employee retention in a tight labor market. The training initiative is expected to deliver measurable outcomes for both employees and the regional economy. This partnership reflects a shared commitment to building a resilient, inclusive and future-ready workforce across Central Minnesota, according to participants. PACE specializes in building employer partnerships that strengthen regional economies and create long-term talent pipelines. Visit the

title: St. G's Bodega Opens On East St. Germain Street Just In Time For FestFall - WJON
content: ST. CLOUD (WJON News) -- A new place to grab some snacks and other essentials is coming to St. Cloud's East End. Marla Waseka owns the building and will operate the community grocery store with her two daughters. The term Bodega is common in urban places like New York City and basically means a small family-owned store or neighborhood convenience shop. It's kind of a gathering space for the neighborhood.  People are welcome to post neighborhood events that are going on.  It's going to provide some basic grocery items, personal care, and household items. She says they want the store to change and evolve as they get feedback from customers and neighbors. What we are creating here is an urban village, which is a place where everything is provided for the residents in the neighborhood.  There are services for them; there are shops, restaurants, and bars.  So eventually we could become a little self-sufficient neighborhood of our own. St. G's Bodega will have four tables and chairs in the front by the windows for people to sit and gather. Eventually they'll offer some prepacked sandwiches and other grab-and-go foods, lunches, etc. The Old Dutch Maid Bakery awning may also be brought out of storage and repurposed in some way in the bread aisle. Waseka says she plans to keep the vibe of a 1920s-era grocery store feel. The St. Cloud City Council approved their tobacco license on Monday night. Maddie Waseka opened The Kitchentte next door to St. G's Bodega a year ago on Festi-Fall weekend. Earlier this year, Marla Waseka bought the former Ace Bar building with plans to renovate that and reopen it as a bar and restaurant in the next few years. title: All of Karol G’s Albums, Ranked - Billboard
content:
From her debut album Unstoppable to No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, see Billboard's ranking. If her debut album title is any indication, Karol G is truly “unstoppable.” Her 2017 set, which includes collaborations with Ozuna on “Hello” and Bad Bunny on “Ahora Me Llama,” instantly placed the Colombian artist on the map as one of the rising woman voices in reggaetón. By her third studio album, KG0516, which became her first No. 1 on the Top Latin Albums chart in 2021, she was a household name. And with her 2023 blockbuster Mañana Será Bonito, she had become a global force to be reckoned with. The latter made history on the Billboard 200 albums chart as the first No. 1 all-Spanish-language album by a woman artist, and won the coveted album of the year award at the 2023 Latin Grammys. Born Carolina Giraldo Navarro, Karol has released seven official studio albums from her 2017 Unstoppable to her most recent, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, out this month. While she’s one to effortlessly experiment with new sounds, such as merengue (“Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido”), dembow (“Ojos Ferrari”), bachata (“Amiga Mía”) and Mexican music (“200 Copas), Karol’s discography has truly captured all of her versions — vulnerable, in love, heartbroken and empowered — throughout the years. That precise evolution is represented in her latest set, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto — a 14-track project where she’s in her feels, mainly powered by nostalgic ballads. NMADST — a sonic steer from her 2025 tropical-heavy album Tropicoqueta — debuted at No. 1 on the Top Latin Albums chart and No. 8 on the Billboard 200 chart. Meanwhile, the new album’s Drake-assisted “Ahí” debuted atop Hot Latin Songs, breaking Bad Bunny’s record-holding streak with “DTMF.” Below, Billboard ranks all of Karol G’s albums, in descending order: Release Date: October 27, 2017On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 2On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 192 On her debut studio album, her first under Universal Music Latino, Karol G dropped some timeless gems including “A Ella,” “Casi Nada,” and the Bad Bunny-assisted “Ahora Me Llama,” which also has a remix with Quavo. In 2017, the reggaetón-pop set became the highest-charting debut set by a woman in more than two years on Top Latin Albums chart, following Chiquis’ Ahora that opened at No. 1 on the chart dated June 20, 2015. Release Date: August 7, 2026On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 1On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 8 Karol G poured all of her feelings into her newest studio album that fittingly translates to “I don’t regret feeling so much.” The 14-track production finds the Colombian artist embracing her emotions like never before, and for the most part, it’s powered by melancholic ballads. Despite introducing her “sad Bichota season,” the album also has some signature reggaetón and dance numbers, such as “Matadora” and “BbY WOW,” the latter of which is in collaboration with Judeline and rusowksy and has quickly become a fan favorite on social media. The set is also home to Karol’s first-ever collabs with both Drake on “Ahí” and Bruno Mars on “Still.” Release Date: June 20, 2025On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 1On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 3 More than just a tropical-leaning album, Tropicoqueta is reflective of Karol’s upbringing in Colombia. “This album is an homage to all those Latin music genres I grew up listening to,” she previously told Billboard Español. “I’m super Colombian, I love Colombia, but more than feeling Colombian, I feel super Latina, like I’m from everywhere,” she continued, which explains why the artist experimented with genres such as reggae, vallenato, mambo, dembow, lambada, Brazilian funk and cumbia on this set. Tropicoqueta (a mix of tropical and flirt) includes collaborations with Marco Antonio Solís, Greeicy and Manu Chao. Release Date: May 3, 2019On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 2On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 54 In contrast to her debut album, the sophomore Ocean was a more introspective look at who Karol G was as a person. We discovered she wears her heart on her sleeves through its title track; that she’s a hopeless romantic on “Créeme” with Maluma; that she can be mischievous on “Culpables” with then-boyfriend and Puerto Rican trap artist Anuel AA — and also naughty on “Punto G.” The set — which the artist created in the beaches of Turks and Caicos — is home to her timeless hits “Pineapple” and “Mi Cama (Remix)” with J Balvin and Nicky Jam. Release Date: March 25, 2021On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 1On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 20 KG0516 (named after her initials and the date she signed her first record deal on May 16) truly unlocked a new era for Karol G. In the 16-track set you’ll find “Tusa,” Karol’s first major collaboration with a mainstream artist, Nicki Minaj, and the official introduction to “Bichota,” the alter ego she created that sparked a movement. On this set, she also slightly started to experiment with other genres outside of reggaetón, delivering an empowering corridos in “200 Copas” and an unapologetic bachata in “El Barco.” Collabs include Camilo, Nathy Peluso, J Balvin and the star-studded “Leyendas” with Wisin y Yandel, Ivy Queen, Nicky Jam and Zion & Alberto Stylee. With this set also came Karol’s electric blue-haired era. Release Date: August 11, 2023On Top Latin Albums: Peaked at No. 1On Billboard 200: Peaked at No. 3 Considered a spinoff to her blockbuster Mañana Será Bonito, Bichota Season not only birthed baby pink-haired Karol, but also 10 songs that became pure girl power anthems, including “BICHOTAG,” “OKI DOKI,” and “S91” (inspired by Psalm 91). On the other hand, with songs such as “Mi Ex Tenía Razón” and “Dispo,” the album wholeheartedly captured the “no effs given” mentality that follows the ending of a relationship and activates “single and ready to mingle” mode. Collaborations on the reggaetón-heavy set include Peso Pluma, Ryan Castro, Young Miko, Kali Uchis and Tiësto. Release Date: February 24, 2023On Top Latin Albums: peaked at No. 1On Billboard 200: peaked at No. 1 The historic Mañana Será Bonito connected with fans at every level possible. A then red-haired Karol G took us through her entire healing process following her very public breakup from Anuel AA, who she dated for nearly three years. The set invited fans on a journey from wanting to get back with an ex in “X Si Volvemos” with Romeo Santos to realizing her self-worth in “TQG” with Shakira, to ultimately giving herself the opportunity to love again in “Tus Gafitas” (a dedication to her love interest Feid at the time). Packed with back-to-back bangers, including “Amargura,” “Cairo,” and “Provenza,” MSB also provides songs such as “Mientras Me Curo del Cora” and the closing title track with Carla Morrison, which offer hopeful and optimistic affirmations. Mañana Será Bonito became the first all-Spanish-language by a woman artist to ever crown the Billboard 200 chart, and it marked the beginning of Karol’s first-ever stadium tour, which grossed $313.3 million and sold 2.3 million tickets across 65 shows, according to Billboard Boxscore. title: State Department Expands Schedule Policy/Career Push as Other Agencies Could Follow - FEDmanager
content: The State Department is reportedly expanding its push to classify more workers into the new Schedule Policy/Career category. According to GovExec, that includes expanding the search to identify more employees in the General Schedule (GS) 13 and GS-14 levels for possible conversion. The move is raising concerns among federal worker groups that other agencies could follow the State Department's approach. This comes after President Trump signed an executive order in June that reclassified approximately 8,000 employees into Schedule P/C, short of the 50,000 or so positions who were projected to possibly move into Schedule P/C. The new category reduces some of the traditional civil service protections available to employees, including protections related to adverse personnel actions. According to one State Department employee who spoke to GovExec, human resources officials at the State Department are “using a short questionnaire to determine if GS-13 and GS-14 level employees are working in policymaking positions that should be reclassified to Schedule P/C.” The questionnaire reportedly includes questions on whether a particular position formulates policy, develops regulations, provides substantive advocacy of foreign policy, represents the department before Congress, as well as other questions. The push to convert more GS-13 and GS-14 employees comes after a senior administration official said that 97 percent of employees converted so far are at GS-15 or higher. The official said a “small number” of GS-13 and GS-14 employees were also converted, but that most of them work at the Office of Management and Budget (OMB). A second staffer told GovExec that while the work is in the early stages, it’s moving “relatively fast.” OPM says the creation of the new category is necessary to ensure that federal employees holding policy making or policy influencing positions “can be held accountable for poor performance or misconduct. “ The creation of Schedule Policy/Career also remains the subject of legal challenges brought by groups including the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), Democracy Forward, and others.

title: Rucsu GS Ammar organises 'July Ziyafat' with cow named 'Baksal', drawing students' backlash over funding - The Business Standard
content: A 'July feast' featuring a cow named 'Baksal' was organised at Rajshahi University (RU) today (15 August), with Rajshahi University Central Students' Union (Rucsu) General Secretary Salauddin Ammar taking a leading role in the event. The feast was held at the university's Central Mosque premises at around 2pm, in which, according to the organisers, some 750 students participated. Students were invited to register through a Google Form. The use of the Rucsu's imagery in the banner for the event drew mixed reactions from the students on social media, with some questioning whether union funds were used to organise the feast. In a Facebook post, RU student Kaushik Das Kangkan said, "Salauddin Ammar is sacrificing a cow in Rucsu's name using the students' money. Who gave him the right to waste their money like this?" However, Rucsu's Debate and Literature Secretary Imran Laskar said that he was unaware whether the cow was being sacrificed on behalf of the student union and denied any involvement in the event. "I want to make it clear that I have no involvement with this event. Those organising it under the Rucsu's banner have not yet given a clear statement about it," he added, urging those involved to clarify the matter to the students. Mehedi Maruf, president of the university unit of Chhatra Odhikar Parishad, questioned the source of funding for the event. "If this is not Rucsu's money, then whose money is it?" he said, alleging that students' money could be being used for political purposes. Several students also criticised the initiative on social media, raising concerns over the quality of food in residential halls, internet services and accommodation facilities. In a video message posted on Facebook last night, Ammar announced the feast and said the cow had been named 'Baksal'. He said the animal would be sacrificed as part of the celebrations, describing the event as a "July Ziyafat" ("July Feast"). Speaking to reporters at the feast, Ammar said today marked what he described as the "historic fall of Baksal" and the second anniversary of the July Uprising, which was why the cow had been given such a name. He said Rucsu had initially promoted the event, but not all union members agreed with it. Later, he alleged, "the cow was gifted by an individual and the union was not involved in the matter". This afternoon, students were seen gathering in small groups near the Central Mosque. Food packets were being prepared inside the Rucsu building, while tarpaulins were being laid on the grass outside the premises for students to sit and eat. The steeper yield backdrop that drew attention this week affects the whole peer group, so the recurring question is which houses are best placed to turn shifting conditions into results across advisory, trading and asset management at once. That framing keeps Goldman in constant comparison with the rest of the large-firm cohort, and it explains why a macro signal touching rates and markets so quickly pulls the name, and its rivals, into the same conversation. The way Goldman Sachs traded this week reflects a wider pattern in how the market reads marquee financial firms. With the broad market near record ground and the daily tape muted, a single macro thread, the climb in Treasury yields, paired with the approach of Federal Reserve minutes, was enough to pull large banks and capital-markets houses into focus. Because such firms sit close to the pulse of rates, dealmaking and trading, they often serve as a gauge of how market participants read corporate confidence and the path of rate decisions. The awaited minutes sharpened that lens, since the document is combed for signals on inflation and the labor market. For a house as prominent as Goldman, being woven into this narrative underscores its role as a bellwether for markets activity and, by extension, for sentiment about the wider economy. The session showed how swiftly attention can gather around a name of this stature when the rate backdrop shifts, even absent fresh company-specific news. title: Could this be the new BMW F 650 GS? - Bike Rider Magazine
content: BMW Motorrad appears to be developing a new middleweight adventure motorcycle that could slot between the F 450 GS and F 800 GS in its global line-up. A test prototype has now been spotted, revealing several similarities to BMW’s existing GS models, although the final production specification remains unclear. The prototype appears to use a parallel-twin engine and shares some technical elements with the recently introduced F 450 GS. However, its chassis and braking components appear closer to those used on BMW’s larger adventure motorcycles, including the F 800 GS and F 900 GS. The motorcycle also runs a 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheel combination, pointing towards stronger off-road capability than the smaller F 450 GS. The engine is currently one of the biggest unanswered questions. BMW could potentially use a heavily revised version of the parallel-twin platform found in the F 450 GS. BMW’s partner TVS already uses a significantly reworked version of this engine in the Norton Atlas, where its 585cc configuration produces 70bhp. It remains unclear whether BMW will use the same displacement or opt for a different configuration. Power could potentially sit in the 65bhp to 70bhp range, although the BMW is expected to have a stronger focus on off-road riding than the Norton Atlas. The prototype’s chassis provides some further clues about its intended role. It uses a steel bridge frame that appears more closely related to the F 900 GS than the F 450 GS, while the braking system also appears to have been derived from BMW’s larger GS models. Combined with the 21-inch front and 18-inch rear wheels, the setup suggests that genuine off-road ability will be an important part of the motorcycle’s character. The motorcycle is still in the early stages of development, with unfinished bodywork particularly noticeable around the front fairing. However, the headlight appears to feature an X-shaped design inspired by the larger R 1300 GS. Interestingly, the familiar GS beak is missing from the prototype. BMW has not yet revealed a name for the new adventure motorcycle. If the engine displacement ends up being close to 600cc, an F 600 GS name could make sense, while BMW could also revive the F 650 GS name previously used for its middleweight adventure models. Given the unfinished state of the prototype, development still appears to be some way from completion. A production version is therefore unlikely to arrive before 2028. If BMW does bring the motorcycle to market, it could eventually compete with models such as the Yamaha Ténéré 700 and the upcoming KTM 690 Rally. title: JPM, GS, MS Stocks Edge Higher After-Hours — Banks Lift Dividends And Announce Buybacks After Fed Stress Test - Stocktwits
content: Shares of JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM), Morgan Stanley (MS) and Goldman Sachs (GS) edged higher in after-hours trading on Wednesday after the banks announced higher dividends and buybacks following the Federal Reserve’s stress test, which showed the banking sector remains well positioned to withstand a severe economic downturn. At the time of writing, JPM stock was up 0.6% after-hours after closing the regular session down 0.21%, while MS shares gained 0.4% and GS stock was up 0.1%. JPMorgan Chase & Co announced a $50-billion share repurchase program and raised its quarterly dividend as part of updated shareholder return plans. The bank said its board also intends to increase its quarterly dividend 10% to $1.65 per share, up from $1.50 per share, for the third quarter of 2026. The new buyback program will take effect from July 1, alongside the updated shareholder return plans. Jamie Dimon, Chairman and CEO of JPMorgan Chase, said, “The Board’s intended dividend increase is supported by our consistent investment in our business and strong financial performance. The new share repurchase program provides us with the flexibility to deploy capital in ways that enhance shareholder value over time.” Goldman Sachs (GS) also increased its quarterly dividend by 11% to $5 per share from $4.50, pointing to strong earnings momentum and a robust capital position. The revised payout implies an annual dividend of $20 and will take effect on July 1, pending board approval. Morgan Stanley (MS) similarly announced a 15% hike in its quarterly dividend to $1.15 per share from $1. In addition, the firm said its board has reauthorized a multi-year share repurchase program of up to $20 billion, with no fixed end date, set to begin in the third quarter. The announcement by JPMorgan Chase & Co comes after the U.S. Federal Reserve released the results of its annual stress test. It showed that large banks are well positioned to withstand a severe recession and continue lending to households and businesses. The Fed said that despite more than $708 billion in total loan losses under the hypothetical scenario, aggregate capital declined only 1.6 percentage points and remained above minimum requirements. It added that all 32 banks tested stayed above their minimum common equity tier 1 capital requirements under a scenario that included a severe global recession, a 39% drop in commercial real estate prices, a 30% fall in house prices and an unemployment rate peaking at 10%. A detailed technical report is expected in the coming months. According to the companies, the system is built to improve efficiency and get more performance out of available computing resources. The platform also incorporates Broadcom's Tomahawk networking technology. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan said the collaboration with OpenAI reflects a long-term effort to build “the physical infrastructure required for the next decade of AI.” He added that the initiative marks the beginning of a “multi-generation roadmap,” with jointly developed silicon aimed at supporting gigawatt-scale data center deployments with Microsoft (MSFT) and other partners starting in 2026. SpaceX shares rose 1% premarket on Wednesday, bucking concerns over rising short interest, lockup-related selling pressure, and a former SEC chair’s warning that IPO excitement could give way to a “great rebalancing.” SPCX stock fell as low as $147.11 early Tuesday, slipping below the $150 level from its first Nasdaq trading day after the June 11 IPO. The stock later recovered, ending Tuesday up about 1% at near $156. About 40 million SpaceX shares are currently sold short, representing roughly 5% to 7% of the company’s publicly tradable float of about 625 million shares, according to S3 Partners. Borrow conditions also do not point to the squeeze pressure. More than 30 million SpaceX shares are available to borrow, while annualized borrowing fees are below 1%, S3 said, according to CNBC. “SPCX has attracted active short-selling interest, but the data suggest this is far from a supply-constrained short,” said Matthew Unterman, head of research at S3. “The current setup looks more like normal price discovery than a classic short-squeeze candidate.” Coatue investor said in a CNBC interview that the firm is not rushing to cash out. When asked whether Coatue would keep or sell its SpaceX shares, he said, “I’m going to keep them,” noting that the shares must be held for six months after receipt. After the lockup, he said the decision becomes “more of a portfolio decision,” based on how large SpaceX becomes relative to the rest of the firm’s holdings. “We own a significant amount of SpaceX,” he said, while adding that some of his biggest mistakes came from “optimizing for the short run.” He pointed to Nvidia as a lesson, calling his decision to sell “one of the bigger mistakes” he had made. “Sometimes you’re like, ‘Oh, maybe I’m so clever. I can sell out of this and buy that.’ It rarely works,” he said. Former SEC Chair Gary Gensler offered a more cautious view, saying that the wave of mega IPOs, including SpaceX, could be a “tell” about where the market cycle stands. He said that markets are funding a major AI infrastructure boom, but warned that some valuations are running at “100, 140 times revenues without earnings,” according to Bloomberg. Gensler said it is possible that the market looks back in six months and finds the IPO wave was “fine.” However, he also warned there is an “equal and better chance” that venture capitalists and sovereign wealth funds begin selling as lockups expire. “I call it the great rebalancing,” Gensler said. “All those venture capitalists and sovereign wealth funds, they’re going to want to take risk off the page.” He said tha investors could move to reduce “a third, a half, maybe three quarters” of their exposure, creating “a lot of selling pressure” as shares become available. Shares of The Wendy’s Company surged more than 20% in overnight trading after a combination of executive leadership changes and intense retail investor activity thrust the restaurant chain into the spotlight. If the gains hold through Wednesday’s session, the stock would be on track for its strongest single-day advance in more than five years. Investor enthusiasm picked up after Wendy’s named two former Potbelly Sandwich executives as its new chief financial officer and chief executive officer, as the beleaguered fast-food chain attempts a hard turnaround. The news quickly became a focal point for traders seeking signs of a broader recovery story. At the same time, online trading communities identified Wendy’s as a potential short-squeeze candidate. The stock climbed to the top of the trending list on Stocktwits and became one of the most talked-about names on Reddit’s WallStreetBets forum. Traders highlighted the company’s profitability, relatively low valuation and sizable dividend yield as reasons the stock differs from some speculative meme-stock names that dominated headlines during the 2021 trading frenzy. Some even argued that a large bearish position in the stock created conditions that could force short sellers to repurchase shares if prices continued rising. Short interest in the stock is at a record level of 26.4%, according to Koyfin data. Such positioning can amplify gains when investors betting against a company rush to close their trades. The stock’s move higher appeared to trigger exactly that dynamic, with buying activity intensifying ahead of Wednesday’s session. The sudden optimism follows a challenging period for the restaurant operator. Wendy’s stock lost nearly 40% over the past year and touched a twenty-year low on Tuesday as consumers cut discretionary spending amid high inflation and fast-food chains competed aggressively on pricing. Wendy’s reported a 5.5% drop in global sales during the first quarter, largely because sales at its existing U.S. restaurants weakened. Profit margins were also squeezed by lower customer traffic and higher food expenses. U.S. same-store sales fell 7.8% in the quarter, worsening from a 2.8% decline a year earlier. title: Why Did Banking Stocks GS, JPM, BAC Surge To 52-Week Highs Today? - Stocktwits
content: Shares of Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (GS), JPMorgan Chase & Co. (JPM), and Bank of America Corp. (BAC) surged to annual highs after the banks posted stellar second-quarter earnings results that beat market expectations. GS stock led the climb among banking stocks, surging more than 9% after its record Q2 results triggered a buy-in. JPM stock rose 2.5% after its results surged past Wall Street expectations, while BAC stock also soared nearly 2% to a record high. GS stock climbed to a record high of $1,143.84 on Tuesday after the company reported record Q2 results that tore past analysts’ expectations. Goldman Sachs posted quarterly revenue of $20.98 billion, significantly higher than Wall Street's $16.4 billion estimate, according to Koyfin data. The investment bank also reported earnings of $15.91 per share, ahead of the $14.40 consensus estimate, while net income reached a record $6.32 billion for the quarter. The strong results were fueled by robust performance in investment banking, equities trading, and asset management, as companies continued to tap capital markets and pursue AI-related financing and strategic deals. "There's a lot of capital out there," CEO David Solomon said in an interview with CNBC on Tuesday. "I'm not concerned about the ability for the capital to be available for things that make sense." GS stock has surged nearly 25% so far this year. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment was ‘extremely bullish’ at the time of writing. JPM stock climbed to a 52-week high of $344.73 on Tuesday, driven by strong Q2 results that boosted investor interest in the company. The bank posted revenue of $57.35 billion versus a consensus estimate of $51.3 billion, while earnings per share (EPS) came in at $7.70 per share versus an expectation of $ 5.80 per share, based on Fiscal.ai data. JPMorgan delivered its strongest trading quarter on record, with trading revenue jumping 35% year over year to $12.1 billion. CEO Jamie Dimon said every business segment achieved record results, noting that market conditions remain favorable for sustained activity. Investment banking fees climbed 30% from a year earlier to $3.3 billion, marking their highest level since 2021, while net interest income rose 10% year over year to $25.6 billion. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs raised the price target on the bank to $418 from $411 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after its Q2 earnings beat, as per TheFly. JPM stock has gained more than 5% so far this year as retail sentiment improved from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over 24 hours. BAC stock also climbed to a record high of $61.21 on Tuesday, driven by Q2 results that demonstrated a strong investment banking pipeline amid growing AI demand. The bank reported revenue of $31.6 billion, ahead of analyst estimates of $30.7 billion. Meanwhile, earnings per share (EPS) came in at $1.21, beating expectations of $1.13 EPS. Investment banking revenue climbed 50% year-over-year, with sales and trading revenue rising 30%. A surge of more than 70% in equities trading was the standout performer, contributing to one of the bank's best quarters in recent years. "We still have very strong pipelines in investment banking. The IPOs and deals are still getting done, and very strong interest in doing transactions,” CEO Brian Moynihan told CNBC in an interview. "The AI buildout still has a lot of debt funding and other funding required, so it's a very good environment." Meanwhile, Jefferies raised the price target on Bank of America to $75 from $70 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares after a "strong quarter," as per TheFly. According to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), the Consumer Price Index (CPI) climbed 3.5% year-on-year, below market expectations. Lower energy costs drove the decline in headline inflation, with the energy index falling 5.7% in June. The softer inflation figures lowered expectations for a rate hike from the Federal Reserve. Shares of Rocket Lab (RKLB) rebounded after a six-session losing streak on Tuesday as CEO Peter Beck highlighted the company as one of the few proven commercial launch providers, calling SpaceX a “friendly rival” and noting that Rocket Lab emerged from a field of more than 100 failed challengers. RKLB stock jumped nearly 3% on Tuesday, with shares also up nearly 2% overnight. In a recent BBC interview, Beck said commercial launch remains exceptionally difficult despite billions of dollars in investment. “Despite billions of dollars and over 100 companies trying, there has actually only been two companies to pop out the other end,” with a regular and reliable launch service, he said, in a discussion that also touched on Rocket Lab’s rivalry with SpaceX. “Launch and a commercial company doing launch still remains extremely rare,” Beck added. Beck called SpaceX a “friendly rival” and said space companies often compete for one contract before working together on another: “You can be competing tooth and tail for a particular contract” and later team up to deliver it, he said. Rocket Lab can also benefit when rivals win as it supplies components such as reaction wheels, star trackers and solar panels.” “We can go head to head with a traditional space prime and then lose,” Beck said. “And then the next day, there’s a purchase order.” Beck called Rocket Lab an end-to-end space company spanning satellites, launch and services from orbit: “We build satellites, we launch them on our rockets and we provide services from space,” he said. Pointing to SpaceX’s Falcon 9 and Starlink model, Beck added: “They’re able to do all those things. And we’re able to do those too.” William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma recently named Rocket Lab and Blue Origin among the strongest challengers to SpaceX, though he said SpaceX still holds more than 90% of the launch market. Rocket Lab is advancing its competitive vertical integration strategy through its $8 billion acquisition of Iridium Communications, which would add a global network, spectrum, and recurring satellite service revenue. The company recently completed a full-duration burn of its Archimedes Vacuum engine, an important step toward the first flight of its reusable Neutron rocket. Rocket Lab said it was “critical preparation for Neutron’s first flight.” Beck has told Stocktwits earlier that Rocket Lab is “pushing very hard” to launch Neutron by the fourth quarter of 2026, while cautioning that the challenge is not merely reaching orbit but proving the rocket can return and be reused. “If we just had to go up, it’s super easy, we’d be in orbit by now,” he previously said. Rocket Lab also completed the U.S. Space Force’s Victus Haze mission, launching 16 hours and 42 minutes after receiving notice and completing spacecraft commissioning and proximity operations ahead of schedule. The company supplied the launch vehicle, spacecraft and orbital operations under one contract, offering a practical demonstration of the integrated model Beck outlined in the interview. Could be an inflection point if positive.” For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com. Comments posted here will also appear on symbol pages. General Fusion Group Ltd. (GFUZ) made history on Monday, becoming the first pure-play nuclear fusion energy company to trade on a major public stock exchange. In an exclusive interview with Stocktwits, CEO Greg Twinney argued that fusion is not just a cleaner alternative to fission but is a fundamentally larger market opportunity. GFUZ stock surged 21% on its debut, added over 25% on Tuesday, and was trading about 2.5% lower in the overnight session. The Vancouver-based company, backed by Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, among others, went public through a SPAC merger with Spring Valley Acquisition Corp. III, which provided General Fusion with approximately $150 million in cash. Earlier, Twinney told the Wall Street Journal that the funding is sufficient to meet the scientific milestones required by its demonstration machine. The listing arrives at a pivotal moment. Surging electricity demand driven by the AI boom, the global spread of electrification, and the energy appetite of large-scale computing has renewed urgency around new sources of firm, clean power. Fusion has attracted growing investment and government attention as a potential long-term answer. According to the Financial Times, the number of private fusion companies has more than doubled over the past five years, intensifying competition at a time when the technology is still roughly a decade from commercialization. General Fusion is targeting its first commercial plant around 2035. Twinney's bull case for fusion starts with what it doesn't produce. Unlike fission, fusion does not generate long-lived radioactive waste, does not use fuels that could be weaponized, and carries no risk of a meltdown. "Fusion is just inherently safe. We're not needing to engineer safety into it in the same way that you need to with fission," he told Stocktwits. "When fusion fails, it kind of just fails safely and there's not really any fallout from that." That safety profile has a direct commercial implication: regulators around the world are moving to govern fusion "in a much lighter way" than conventional nuclear, Twinney said, which he believes creates the potential to site fusion plants closer to population centers and industrial demand. That's a significant advantage over fission, which requires remote, heavily secured facilities. "We get all the benefits that fission can provide without the downsides," he said. There's another significant advantage. Fusion reactors primarily use deuterium, which can be extracted from seawater and is "massively abundant." The other component, tritium, is rarer in nature but can be bred through the interaction of a neutron and lithium. Fission, by contrast, relies on uranium and other finite sources. "The overall market size because of the safety profile and the abundance of fuel in fusion is much bigger than fission," Twinney said. While advanced nuclear companies such as Oklo Inc. (OKLO) and NuScale Power Corp. (SMR) are often thought of as being closer to commercialization than fusion technology, Twinney said that the gap may not be as large as investors assume. While the road to commercialization for fusion technology has its challenges, including achieving reactor durability, tritium fuel breeding, economic viability, and the ability to efficiently extract and convert fusion energy into electricity, he argues small modular reactor (SMR) timelines also struggle with regulatory hurdles that can make timelines less predictable than they appear today. "I know that the timelines for SMRs, which can be very unpredictable due to regulations and those types of things, [are] probably not that different," he said. According to Twinney, the combination of abundant fuel supplies and a lighter regulatory framework could ultimately enable fusion to scale faster than conventional nuclear technologies once commercial viability has been demonstrated. However, Twinney does not view fusion and fission as mutually exclusive technologies. "They will be complementing each other," he said. "And I think that fusion kind of rounds out the nuclear circle if you think about it that way," he added. When asked about criticism from former Commonwealth Fusion Systems CTO Dan Brunner, who, in a recent interview with the Financial Times, said General Fusion's commercialization timeline was "very hard to believe," Twinney said the company’s timelines were based on real experimental results from its Lawson Machine 26. The machine is designed to demonstrate that plasma can be heated through mechanical compression rather than superconducting magnets or high-powered lasers, he said, adding that the company's early results validated the operating principles behind its MTF approach that are “not based on fiction or papers being written.” The timelines “are based on our real results from machines that we have built and operated and then eventually written papers on. But those are real results papers, not theoretical papers,” he said. Twinney also emphasized that General Fusion's approach could offer a cost advantage over many competing technologies. While many other fusion developers rely on expensive superconducting magnets, high-powered lasers, or advanced materials that have yet to be proven at commercial scale, General Fusion's Magnetized Target Fusion (MTF) system uses mechanical compression and a liquid-lithium wall that can protect reactor components from neutron damage, help with breeding tritium fuel, and absorbing fusion energy as heat that can be converted into electricity using conventional steam turbines. In an earlier interview with Stocktwits, Chief Strategy Officer Megan Wilson had also pointed to the economic advantages of MTF, which eliminate the need for expensive magnets, targets, lasers, or exotic, not-yet-invented materials. The technology also eliminates the need for frequent replacement of components damaged by neutron exposure, she had said. “Our plants are designed to be cost-competitive compared to coal, steam, and natural gas,” she had said then. “They are expected to deliver four times as much energy per unit of fuel as fission, without long-lived radioactive waste, positioning them as the superior nuclear technology for sustainable growth.” By avoiding costly magnets and lasers and using existing industrial technologies, Twinney said he believes General Fusion has a clearer path to building an economically viable power plant, as the company’s design has from the beginning aimed to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion. "What we are trying to do at General Fusion, and our power plant design from the beginning, has been we want to avoid the major barriers to commercializing fusion.
